prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1408; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name in this format, so I'll answer the other questions. Let the record reflect that the witness is the plaintiff in this matter.

Q: Ms. or Mr. [Plaintiff], let me ask you directly. Where were you on the afternoon of the collision?

A: I was driving home from work on a two-lane road in Pearland, Texas. It was a clear afternoon, and traffic was moderate.

Q: Describe what happened immediately before the impact.

A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction drifted into my lane as it went around a slow truck. I tapped my brakes and turned slightly to the right, but there wasn't time to avoid it entirely. The front of our cars made contact.

Q: How fast were you traveling?

A: I'd say around twenty-five miles an hour. It wasn't fast. I remember the airbags did not deploy, and both cars were drivable, though mine was towed.

Q: Did you feel any pain at the scene?

A: Not right away. I was shaken up and mostly worried about the other driver. By the next morning my neck was stiff, and by the second day I could barely turn my head to check my mirrors.

Q: What treatment did you receive?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic the day after the accident, and then I followed up with my primary care doctor. I was given muscle relaxers, told to apply heat, and referred to physical therapy. I've attended about two sessions a week since then.

Q: Have you missed any work because of your neck?

A: I missed a few days at the beginning, and since then I've been working modified hours. Sitting at a desk for long stretches makes it worse.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?

A: Simple things are harder. I can't carry groceries on my left side without discomfort, I've stopped playing my weekend recreational league, and sleeping through the night is difficult. I try to keep up with my physical therapy exercises at home.

Q: Have you had any prior neck problems?

A: No, not that I can recall. I had no treatment for my neck before this accident.
